_comment: The jury. Half of every quality score comes from here, so who sits on it is published, not implied.
The rule that matters: a judge must come from a DIFFERENT model family than the models being judged.
A model scoring its own family is a conflict of interest, and no amount of prompt wording fixes it.
Neither Anthropic nor z.ai models appear in providers.json, so neither judge is scoring a relative.
More than one judge, from more than one family, is what makes the score arguable instead of an
opinion. bench/agreement.py measures how much they agree and publishes it - including, deliberately,
when they do not. A disagreement between judges is more informative than a confident average.
`via` says how a judge is reached, and it is an honesty field, not a config one:
api    - anyone with a key can reproduce this judge exactly.
manual - scored by hand through a chat interface, not by API. NOT reproducible by a stranger, and METHOD.md says so.
Prefer api. An agent judge is acceptable only alongside at least one api judge.

judges.name: glm
judges.note: Reachable on the coding-plan endpoint; the general paas/v4 endpoint answered HTTP 429 on 2026-09-06. Thinking is switched OFF: with it on, the model spends the whole token budget reasoning and returns an EMPTY message - 3 of the first 4 calls failed that way. Off, it answers in 1.7s using 42 tokens instead of 11.8s and 238. A judge that thinks out loud is not a better judge, it is an unanswered call.

judges.name: claude
judges.note: Scored by hand through a chat interface, so a stranger cannot reproduce this judge's scores exactly. Declared as a limitation in METHOD.md rather than hidden. Run judge.py --api with two API judges to get a fully reproducible jury.
